header: Date: 2026-07-21 11:00 PDT | Duration: 42 mins | Attendees: Nina Patel (Redwood AE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Karen Bishop (Apex Head of AI), Marco Diaz (Apex Platform Eng), Sasha Li (Apex PM)
transcript: [00:00] Nina Patel: Okay, good morning everyone, thanks for joining. This is the final weekly sync for the Apex pilot, we're gonna run through the results, remaining risks, and next steps for signoff.
[00:22] Karen Bishop: Thanks Nina. Quick heads up — we have a few execs on standby for the 7/28 wrap, so today is kinda the last formal check before we escalate.

[00:35] Samir Rao: Awesome. I'll start with a short recap of the test matrix, throughput, and the 95th latency across the three profiles we ran — hosted, dedicated with 2xA10s, and a quantized private run.

[01:05] Marco Diaz: Real quick — the load we used was synthetic traffic based on our cart recommender pattern, roughly 120 rps peak per shard, with bursts to 250 for 30s. That was the baseline for all tests.

[01:30] Samir Rao: Right. Results: hosted API median latency was ~120ms, 95th ~310ms under burst. Dedicated (2xA10) median 85ms, 95th ~170ms. Private quantized run had lower cost per token but we saw tail latency variability — likely due to kernel fallback on one of the nodes.
[02:10] Sasha Li: When you say kernel fallback, is that the quantization path? We saw some spikes in the dashboard and weren't sure if that's expected in close-to-prod.

[02:25] Samir Rao: Yes — the quantized path uses alternate kernels and sometimes falls back to float kernels for certain ops; that produced a few ~400ms spikes. We recommend pinning the model variant for production or using Redwood Dedicated which had more stable 95th percentile.
[03:00] Karen Bishop: Understood. From a business case perspective, our target was 95th < 200ms and cost less than $0.20 per 1k tokens for the high-volume path. Do these runs satisfy that?

[03:18] Samir Rao: Dedicated meets the latency target comfortably (95th ~170ms). Cost per 1k tokens for Dedicated, amortizing reserved commit, comes in around $0.16 in our modeled workload. Hosted is slightly higher for sustained volume due to egress and multi-tenant premiums.

[03:50] Marco Diaz: That cost model assumed the batching heuristics stayed as-is; on our real traffic pattern, the prefix caching reduced effective tokens by ~12% which pushes cost down further — so the $0.16 is conservative.
[04:10] Nina Patel: Good point. We included the prefix/KV caching estimate in the final spreadsheet, will send updated numbers after you share the last week's real logs.
[04:30] Karen Bishop: Security questions: SOC2 is a must, and we need to verify KMS integration for key separation. Also wanna confirm SSO and RBAC flows for the team.

[04:45] Nina Patel: We have SOC2 Type II docs, pen-test summary, and the KMS integration guide — we'll share all that in the doc bundle. For SSO we support SAML and OIDC; RBAC is role scoped by team and route. I'll attach the diagrams.
[05:10] Marco Diaz: On the VPC/private side, latency was slightly higher due to network hops, is that expected? The private deploy had 95th ~190ms in our run.

[05:25] Samir Rao: A bit expected — private deployments can have extra latency depending on networking and placement. We tuned kernel selection and batching but if you want, Redwood can co-locate nodes with your VPC or bring Dedicated into your region which reduces that delta.
[06:00] Sasha Li: Are there any outstanding data residency or logging issues? We need audit logs for compliance and retention of 13 months.

[06:15] Nina Patel: Audit logs are available and configurable; we can set retention and export to your SIEM. We also offer an on-prem control plane variant if regulated data needs to be fully air-gapped.

[06:40] Karen Bishop: Great. From a success criteria doc standpoint, I want the final page to clearly state the metrics we'll measure for signoff: 95th latency < 200ms, error rate < 0.5%, cost per 1k tokens < $0.18, and UAT acceptance on a 50k session sample. Can someone capture that as the canonical list?
[07:05] Nina Patel: I'll update the success criteria and circulate. We already have a signoff checklist in the shared drive — I'll make the thresholds explicit.

[07:20] Samir Rao: Quick note on reliability: we exercised failover routing in the Dedicated config. During a simulated node outage, we saw <2% request retry and no full-service degradation — the KV cache warmed back up in about 12s.
[07:45] Marco Diaz: That warm-up is fine as long as it happens predictably. We'll include a short SLO doc in operations for how we want cache priming to behave.

[08:05] Sasha Li: On the model quality side, our A/B eval against the baseline recommender showed a +6% conversion uplift in the sample set. There were a few edge cases with personalization tokens being truncated — I think that was due to a max sequence length mismatch?

[08:35] Samir Rao: Yes, during the config we had a mismatch between your tokenizer settings and the model's sequence window, that caused truncation. We patched the prompt template and reran the eval; new run shows truncation resolved.
[09:00] Karen Bishop: For procurement and legal: can Redwood accept our standard MSA with a minimal redline, or do you need a specific addendum around data processing?

[09:15] Nina Patel: Redwood's legal can accept most standard MSAs; we usually add a short DPA addendum for data processing and options for KMS. I'll coordinate with our contracts team and follow up with a draft redline.
[09:40] Marco Diaz: Also, performance guarantee language — we need some SLA commitment on latency targets once we go into Dedicated. Is that in the dedicated contract?
[09:55] Nina Patel: Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency and uptime targets in the enterprise addendum. We'll include the 95th latency floor in the SLA and define remediation steps.
[10:12] Sasha Li: Anything else on tooling? We liked the per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdown in the console — that helps our finance team forecast spend.
[10:25] Nina Patel: Good to hear. We can give a walkthrough for your finance and ops teams in the wrap-up session if helpful.
[10:40] Karen Bishop: Let's talk risks quickly — one remaining risk is model drift over time and cost creep if traffic pattern changes. How do you support detect+alert for regressions?

[10:55] Samir Rao: Redwood Optimize has regression alerting tied to eval prompt sets; you can configure thresholds and automatic rollback to a safe variant. We can set that up during onboarding and run weekly evals against production snapshots.
[11:20] Marco Diaz: For the production cutover, we want a canary for 10% traffic for 48 hours before a full rollout and automatic rollback on quality or latency breaches.
[11:35] Nina Patel: That's a standard rollout pattern we support — canary, ramp, automatic fallback to hosted or previous variant per policy.
[12:00] Karen Bishop: Anything from the Redwood ops side on scaling? Our peak season will double traffic in Nov and we need a clear scaling plan.

[12:15] Samir Rao: Reserved Dedicated capacity can be configured with burst policy; you can provision baseline commit and have burstable spare capacity. We'll include recommended commit levels in the spreadsheet.
[12:35] Sasha Li: Regarding final numbers, can you break down expected monthly bill at 2x and 3x baseline traffic? Finance wants a sensitivity table.
[12:50] Nina Patel: Yes, we'll append a sensitivity table (2x/3x/5x) in the cost model and include token amortization and reserved discount assumptions.
[13:10] Karen Bishop: On integration tasks, Marco will be our lead. He'll need the runbook for key rotation, KMS, and SSO. Marco, confirm that you got the runbook after this call.
[13:25] Marco Diaz: Yep, will confirm. I'll also run one more load test with the final prompt template on 7/22 and share results.

[14:00] Nina Patel: Ok, so to recap — Dedicated meets latency target and cost model looks favorable when including prefix caching; security/compliance artifacts will be shared; legal next steps for contract redline. Any objections to moving forward to exec wrap-up and contract phase?
[14:20] Karen Bishop: No objections from me, provided the final doc bundle has the explicit thresholds and the finance sensitivity table.
[14:35] Sasha Li: I'm good, pending Marco's final load test.
[14:45] Nina Patel: Great. We'll send the spreadsheet and SOC2 package tomorrow. Samir, you'll send the short ops runbook?
[15:00] Samir Rao: Yes — runbook, KV cache notes, failover steps. I'll include the known quantization caveats and recommended model pinning settings.
[15:20] Karen Bishop: One last question about backups and logs retention — can we export logs to our GCS bucket with encryption via our KMS?
[15:35] Nina Patel: Yes, logs export is supported and can be encrypted using your KMS keys; we'll include the integration steps in the security doc.
[16:00] Marco Diaz: Thanks. I'll share the final throughput numbers and the result of the 7/22 run. If those look good, we'll be ready for 7/28.
[16:18] Nina Patel: Perfect. I'll schedule the 7/28 exec wrap and get the legal thread started. Thanks everyone.
[16:30] (call wraps, small crosstalk)
[41:30] End of recording
